Subject: Renewal + capacity top-up request (Nexa)

Hi Tessa,

Our renewal is coming up next month and we'd like to include a reserved pool top-up in the term. We're targeting +40 GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) to support a spike in batch and realtime inference for a new feature launch. Key asks:

- Confirm throughput guarantees for the expanded pool (tokens/sec and concurrent request guidance).
- We need predictable latency for our interactive use; can Redwood provide a firm 95th percentile latency SLO post-rollout?
- Because this is a bump on renewal, our infra team wants a temporary SLA concession during the ramp (we expect a 6–12 week warm-up while caches and traffic shaping settle). Specifically, we'd like an SLA grace period with limited uptime/latency credits while the new capacity is stabilized.

I've attached a short capacity worksheet (capacity_request.xlsx) with our expected traffic mix and a proposed schedule. Can you confirm what pricing delta and SLA language we'd need to sign? We'd prefer a single contract amendment at renewal instead of separate addenda.

Thanks,
Asha Menon

Hi Asha — quick technical note from infra:

Thanks for the traffic worksheet — useful. A few practical recommendations for the +40 GPU expansion:

- Staged rollout (recommended): Provision +15 GPUs as canary for 2 weeks, then +25 GPUs in week 3 if KPIs look good. This reduces risk and lets us warm both prefix/KV caches and your model shard placements.
- Latency SLOs: Given the ramp, we can commit to a 95th percentile latency SLO of 120ms post-stabilization on the dedicated pool for your interactive endpoints. During the ramp period we usually allow a temporary uplift (on the order of +30–50ms) while caches fill and autoscaling policies are tuned.
- Throughput guarantees: We can offer a throughput floor expressed as guaranteed concurrent requests per GPU (we'll map this to tokens/sec after we confirm sequence-length distribution).

I'll attach a filled capacity workbook with a staged schedule and suggested rollout milestones. If you have a preferred canary timebox shorter than 2 weeks, let us know — we can compress, but risk/reachability goes up.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tessa / Marcus — this is helpful, thank you. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can accept a staged rollout as you describe. Our expected launch window is mid-November, so timeline aligns.
- For the SLA grace period, our legal/ops prefer a defined interim where latency SLOs are non-punitive and uptime credits are limited until stabilization. - Pricing: please include a line-item for the reserved top-up and a one-time onboarding fee to cover migration & tuning. We'd like the final amendment to be a single DocuSign (renewal + top-up + SLA amendment).

Can you confirm whether Redwood requires any further operational data (e.g., production p95 baseline, token distribution) to finalize the throughput guarantees? Finance is copied for visibility.

Thanks,
Asha

Asha — thanks, and appreciate the clear ask from legal/ops. Below is our proposed commercial and SLA handling for the renewal package (summary):

1) Commercials
- Reserved top-up: +40 GPUs (A100 equiv) added to your Dedicated pool for a 12-month term at the renewal price agreed in the attached proposal. Discount: 18% off public list on the top-up incremental units.
- One-time onboarding/tuning fee: $42,500 (covers canary run, model shard optimization, and a 2-week on-call tuning window).

2) SLA grace / exception (requested)
- Grace period: 90 days from the first day of production traffic on the expanded pool. During this period:
  - Latency SLO: advisory only (we will monitor and provide operational guidance); formal latency SLA and related financial credits are suspended.
  - Uptime credits: capped at 10% credit in month 1, 5% credit in month 2, and standard credit policy applies thereafter. (Note: we proposed slightly higher credit cap for month 1 to compensate for potential migration risk; happy to discuss if Nexa prefers the 5% cap you proposed.)
- Milestones: We will track stabilization via two objective metrics (p95 latency improvement trend and error-rate trend) with weekly checkpoints. If stabilization completes earlier, SLA clauses revert to standard terms upon mutual agreement.

3) Technical safeguards
- We will provision an initial +15 GPU canary for 14 days, then expand the remainder after a joint validation window.
- Redwood will enable priority routing for Nexa's realtime traffic during the ramp and run prefix caching. Marcus will share a short runbook for the on-call tuning week.

4) Next steps
- I will upload the finalized amendment and pricing to HubSpot and route the DocuSign envelope for signature (renewal + top-up + SLA amendment in one document).
- Legal: please review the SLA exception wording in the attached draft (SLA_Schedule_Amendment_draft.docx) and send any redlines within 3 business days.

If this looks acceptable, we'll generate the DocuSign this week and target a mid-November activation.

Best regards,
